Library animation and worked-solution visual review

How to use the revised problems

Read the problem and its complete written solution. Where a visual process helps, the solution now contains an inspectable diagram or model. Use Previous step and Next step to follow one operation at a time. Play runs the stored steps; Restart restores the first step. The caption explains the currently displayed operation. All models start paused.

A question-linked aid uses its stated values, displayed mathematical objects or a clearly labeled derived witness. A supporting concept model uses a separate teaching example and states that its numerical values are not this problem’s answer. Symbolic arguments retain their complete written proofs when an additional model would not clarify them. Existing examination schematics and source links remain available.

What changed

  • All 35 chapters use the shared boundary and padding review. Arrowheads are smaller, connections follow actual node boundaries, labels use measured glyph dimensions, and colliding annotations are separated.
  • Merge records and transposed entries use separate travel lanes where a straight path obscured other labels. Saved mathematical checkpoints are unchanged.
  • 317 question-linked aids show exact row operations, Karnaugh covers, multiplexer inputs, gate-level equivalence miters, actual AND-tree arrival bounds, ripple carries, program object updates, array movements, probability masses and other relevant constructions.
  • 74 arrays/list teaching aids and 1362 supporting concept placements explain applicable methods with explicitly separate examples. These placements reuse 133 different subject-specific concept models; they are not that many distinct new models.
  • The 2085 original problem statements, options, complete solution bodies and source labels remain intact. The revision adds visual teaching and operation-specific captions without replacing complete reasoning with a picture.

Open representative examples

  • Combinational circuits: questions 37–48 show gate-level miters; questions 49–58 show the three actual arrival-sensitive AND trees; questions 59–68 show fixed-width ripple addition.
  • Karnaugh maps: question-linked ON/DC specifications and selected optimal covers.
  • Gaussian elimination: exact rational row operations with a visible coefficient/right-hand-side boundary.
  • Functions and parameter passing: independent objects, aliases, persistent storage and helper composition.
  • Array programming: overlapping reads/writes, shifts, prefix sums and in-place dependencies.

What was verified

The actual browser rendered 272 existing animation models at 1534 saved checkpoints and checked 1044 intermediate movement samples. The problem aids passed geometry checks at 1790 stored visual steps. Tests measured label bounds, text collisions, rectangular padding and annotated connector endpoints. All 35 chapter pages loaded their problem models, retained their problem counts, stayed within a 390-pixel mobile page width and exposed written solutions in print mode. Mathematical glyphs use STIX Two Math; algorithms retain JetBrains Mono.

Independent exact arithmetic checks cover the implemented row reductions, carry results, mux cofactors, miter truth values and replayed program contracts. Visual spot checks include the miter schematic, Karnaugh map, Gaussian matrix and aliasing diagram. These are finite checks. They do not certify every unsampled transient, every editable laboratory input or every mathematical assertion in the original library. This delivery reviews visual instruction; it does not claim a new exhaustive proof audit or guaranteed performance on future examinations.
